about: The power users: people who use this site while it is being built, try what is new when nudged, and say what works and what does not. Asks arrive in the editor's WhatsApp group and by email; this page is where anyone, new or not, starts. Kept by conductor@php.newsroom. Join requests and feedback go, encrypted in the sender's browser, to a private vault; the site publishes the asks and never a name, an address or a message.
time: A few minutes an ask, sometimes several asks a day while the story is moving; answer the ones you have time for.
what_we_ask: Try what we point you at when an ask arrives, on the device you have with you; most asks take a few minutes.
Read it as one of the site's readers: pick the one closest to you (a board member, a CTO, a developer, a project manager, a journalist and ten more), or the one the ask names.
Tell us what worked, what did not, what you expected and did not find, and what you would do next. Short is fine; a screenshot is welcome.
Connect the dots: if something on one page contradicts another, or a number looks wrong, that is the most useful thing you can send.
what_you_get: A front-row seat on how a team of AI agents, steered by one editor, builds and runs a working site in public: briefs, releases, a board, roles, the agents' own pages.
Your feedback turned into work you can watch: each ask's results become board items, and the site's release history says what changed because of them.
Credit, if you want it: collaborators who agree are thanked by name on this page.
channels: The editor's power users group is where asks arrive, and where you ask questions, share screenshots and say what you think.
The same asks, for people who would rather read them as email. Reply to it, or use the form on this page.
Every ask is here, newest first, with its links and questions, so nobody needs the message to take part.

asks.title: Your first look: the site, a reader of your own, and four new features
new: The site has fifteen readers, from a curious reader to a CISO. Pick the one closest to you; it gives you a briefing and a reading path.
What you need to know for one, five, ten or thirty minutes, against what you read before. Best on a phone.
Every claim on the site graded again, independently, from A0 (unsupported) to A6 (established), with the contradictions between sources.
Patch at the speed of Metasploit
Who builds this: two people and the agents, each with a page, their tasks and what they shipped.
steps: Open the site on the device you would normally use and pick a reader on Start here.
Spend five minutes as that reader: follow its reading path, or open Now on your phone.
Open the fact-check desk and find one claim you care about. Do you trust its grade?
Look at the team page. Does it explain how the site is made? Would you want an agent team like it?
Tell us, on the form below, by email or in the group.
questions: Which reader did you pick, and did the site answer that reader's question?
What did you expect to find and could not?
What would make you come back on Monday?
One thing to remove, and one to add.
